page: Amazon Web Services c8in.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and Intel x86_64 hardware. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz, utilizing 2 threads per core. System memory totals 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data operations. Dedicated hardware accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero. Network connectivity features a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps along with EBS optimization, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Relative to its hardware footprint, the instance allocates cost toward high-frequency dedicated compute capacity and baseline network throughput rather than large local disk or high memory pools. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio restricts use cases requiring in-memory data processing, focusing efficiency on workloads where processing frequency is the primary constraint. Applicable workloads include batch compute, distributed microservices, network-bound web servers, and front-end application tiers.
